_notes: output_modalities=all lists every model group (chat, image, embeddings, rerank, video, speech, transcription, decisions); without it /models only returns text models.
Decisions are at /api/alpha/decisions: the base URL with /v1 replaced by /alpha.
Images and image edits both POST /images; edits are JSON with the pictures as data URLs in input_references, and no mask (endpoints.imageEdit).
Image and video options come per model from /images/models and /videos/models; suggest covers what no list gives. /audio/speech only returns mp3 or pcm (pcm does not play in the page).
guide is the text of the Providers tab: how hard the setup is (level 1-4 and ease), a summary, the steps, and what is good or to watch. Shown with the signup link.
label: OpenRouter

signup.text: No key? Get one at OpenRouter

guide.summary: Sign in, add credit, make a key. Every model is switched on from the start, so there is nothing else to set up.
steps: Sign in at openrouter.ai, for example with your Google account.
Add credit under Credits (pay as you go).
Create a key under Keys and paste it at the top of this page.
good: All models are available at once, with nothing to enable.
Works straight from this page (GitHub Pages), no server needed.
Has every tab here, including video and rerank.
watch: Pay as you go: the key spends your credit, so set a limit on the key if you share it.

_notes: The Video Generator and Animate the DreamGen Scene offer only these models, in this order. Each was run for real on OpenRouter (dates below); the Video tab still lists every video model.
Durations, resolutions and aspect ratios come from /videos/models; a list here narrows them to what was tested or works. default is what the tools start with: the cheapest tested settings.

frames: the frame images the model takes. needsFirstFrame: refuses text-only jobs. audio: "off" (none), "optional" (generate_audio false works), "always" (an audio track every time). faces: what happened with a photoreal face as the first frame (2026-11-08 research, #26).
tested: what was run, with the price billed. Test frames were plain gradients, 1024x576 PNG.

priceSeen: shown next to the price when a test was billed differently from the listed price. priceFactor: the estimate is multiplied by it, so the price scale follows what was really billed. The tools show the provider's listed price, or a 1-5 scale ($$$$$) where only an estimate is possible (token prices, or a priceFactor); amounts from our tests are never shown.

Taken out on 2026-11-09: google/veo-3.1-lite and bytedance/seedance-2.0-mini refuse AI-generated faces too, even a clearly non-human one (an alien with head ridges), not only photoreal ones, which makes them no use for DreamGen scenes. They still worked for text-to-video and frames without faces (Veo: first and last frame, audio off, 4 s 720p for $0.12; Seedance: 4 s 480p for about $0.14), and stay usable under Other video model.
